","candidate_answer":"1. “What does not kill me makes me stronger.” — **Friedrich Nietzsche**, *Twilight of the Idols*

2. “One must still have chaos in oneself to be able to give birth to a dancing star.” — **Friedrich Nietzsche**, *Thus Spoke Zarathustra*

3. “In the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer.” — **Albert Camus**, *Return to Tipasa*

4. “One must imagine Sisyphus happy.” — **Albert Camus**, *The Myth of Sisyphus*

5. “Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.” — **Marcus Aurelius**, *Meditations*

6. “The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.” — **Marcus Aurelius**, *Meditations*

7. “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.” — **Epictetus**, *Enchiridion*

8. “First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.” — **Epictetus**, *Discourses*

9. “We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.” — **Seneca**, *Moral Letters to Lucilius*, Letter 13

10. “While we are postponing, life speeds by.” — **Seneca**, *Moral Letters to Lucilius*, Letter 1

11. “The unexamined life is not worth living.” — **Socrates**, in Plato’s *Apology*

12. “We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.” — **Aristotle**, *Nicomachean Ethics*

13. “He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.” — **Laozi**, *Tao Te Ching*, Chapter 33

14. “When we see men of worth, we should think of equalling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves.” — **Confucius**, *Analects*, 4.17

15. “All things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.” — **Baruch Spinoza**, *Ethics*

16. “For to be possessed of a vigorous mind is not enough; the prime requisite is rightly to apply it.” — **René Descartes**, *Discourse on Method*

17. “All the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.” — **Blaise Pascal**, *Pensées*

18. “Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.” — **Søren Kierkegaard**, *The Concept of Anxiety*

19. “Life swings like a pendulum to and fro between pain and boredom.” — **Arthur Schopenhauer**, *The World as Will and Representation*

20. “Man is condemned to be free.” — **Jean-Paul Sartre**, *Existentialism Is a Humanism*

21. “To will oneself free is also to will others free.” — **Simone de Beauvoir**, *The Ethics of Ambiguity*

22. “Have courage to use your own understanding!” — **Immanuel Kant**, *An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?*

23. “Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.” — **John Stuart Mill**, *On Liberty*

24. “Man is born free; and everywhere he is in chains.” — **Jean-Jacques Rousseau**, *The Social Contract*

25. “Curiosity is the lust of the mind.” — **Thomas Hobbes**, *Leviathan*

26. “He who fears he shall suffer, already suffers what he fears.” — **Michel de Montaigne**, *Essays*

27. “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.” — **Ludwig Wittgenstein**, *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus*

28. “The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge.” — **Bertrand Russell**, *What I Believe*

29. “My experience is what I agree to attend to.” — **William James**, *The Principles of Psychology*
